sources.beginner: Prompt names the Suite Capital Portfolio Studio: funded set, Risked EMV and Success-case NPV cards (OptimizationResults.jsx:53-54) and per-project EMV (CapitalPortfolioStudio.jsx:387) all print via formatCurrency with maximumFractionDigits 0 (OptimizationResults.jsx:13, CapitalPortfolioStudio.jsx:228). Exact values need the hand method of beginner m06/l02. NextGen CapitalExplorer is OKONO-only (select fields, no editable inventory).
sources.intermediate: Prompt names the Suite AFE Cost Control Manager: per-line forecast and variance print as whole USD (CostBreakdownTab.jsx:146, :219, :232), the dashboard EAC is compact notation, CPI and SPI tiles toFixed(2) (AFEDashboard.jsx:39, :57), and the dashboard evaluates at todayIsoDate() (AFEDashboard.jsx:115), so planned value and SPI as of 2028-10-03 are not shown. Earned value, planned value, CPI and SPI are hand-calcs taught in intermediate m03-m04 and m06/l02. NextGen CostExplorer is OFON-1 only.
sources.advanced: Portfolio risk from the Capital Portfolio Studio's seeded Monte Carlo: P(loss) toFixed(1) percent and P90/P10 as whole $MM (OptimizationResults.jsx:59, :65); stdDev is the closed form taught in advanced m02/l02 (the app prints it only as a whole number in the correlation note, :95); partner and operator billing from JVPartnerManagement.jsx:139/:188 (toLocaleString, up to 3 decimals).

fix.display: src/components/capitalportfoliostudio/OptimizationResults.jsx:13 and :53-54, :130 and src/pages/apps/CapitalPortfolioStudio.jsx:228, :387 -> formatCurrency for these $MM figures prints 4 decimals (minimumFractionDigits 4, maximumFractionDigits 4) on the Risked EMV and Success-case NPV cards, the funded-project table EMV column and the inventory EMV column

fields.recommendation: Display fix. The prompt names the Capital Portfolio Studio and asks for four decimals, but every $MM figure there is Intl.NumberFormat with maximumFractionDigits 0, so a learner who reads the Studio misses tol 0.001 on every beginner field. Today the fields are recoverable only by hand (risk each row, take the funded set the Studio names, and sum exact inputs, taught in beginner m06/l02); a tolerance change cannot help without reaching 0.5 million USD.
fields.evidence: With Full precision on, prints at 4 decimals (jest: capitalportfoliostudio/__tests__/w3FullPrecision.test.jsx, the engine result through formatFull, checked against the key first).

fields.evidence: Per-line variance printed as whole USD; sum -301,285 exactly (budget 23,752,475 less EAC). The dashboard subtext is compact and would fail.
The Suite AFE screens never print earned value. Budget x progress by line, as taught: 7,684,638.75 + 2,963,180 + 708,636 + 1,203,176.25 + 0 = 12,559,631 exactly.
Time progress 211/319 days (2028-03-06 to 2028-10-03 over the window) x budget 23,752,475 = 15,710,884.72, taught in m04/l03; nearest USD 15,710,885 is within 0.5.

fields.evidence: Closed form taught in m02/l02: stdDev = sqrt(sum var + rho x ((sum sd)^2 - sum var)) over the mixture sds of the set funded at 640, rho 0.45; spreadsheet-exact. The Studio shows it only inside the correlation note as a whole number ($219).
fields.notes: Recommend printing stdDev at 4 decimals alongside the P90 fix so the app route also passes.

fields.evidence: Card prints (probLoss x 100).toFixed(1) = 2.8% and the engine value is exactly 0.028 (a count over the default iterations), so 0.028 passes tol 5e-5.
fields.notes: Passes only because this count lands on a 0.1 percent step; the card's resolution (0.001 as a fraction) is coarser than the four decimals the prompt asks. Worth printing toFixed(2) percent with the P90 display fix.

fields.evidence: Partner share printed with toLocaleString() default (up to 3 decimals): 2,505,615.3; also 0.186 x 13,471,050 by hand. Nearest USD 2,505,615 is 0.3 away, inside tol 0.5.
Operator amount printed 4,714,867.5 (0.35 x 13,471,050). Rounded to the nearest USD it is 4,714,867 or 4,714,868, each exactly 0.5 away, which equals tol 0.5.
fields.notes: Boundary: the prompt's 'nearest unit' lands exactly on a half, so a learner passes only because tol equals half a unit and the grader compares with <=. Typing the printed 4714867.5 passes exactly. Safe as long as the grader stays numeric (exact) arithmetic.
